relations.myth: Trojan service and mission through the Rutulian lines
relations.note: They follow Aeneas and volunteer to carry news to him.
Aeneas awards Euryalus victory prizes and gives Nisus a consolation shield.
They compete in the footrace held in Anchises’ honor.

relations.myth: Mission from the besieged Trojan camp
relations.note: They present their mission to Ascanius and undertake to reach Aeneas.
Ascanius gives Euryalus his sword and promises rewards and maternal protection.
Aletes praises their courage and interprets it as divine favor.

relations.myth: Council in the besieged Trojan camp
relations.note: Mnestheus shares the command and council setting with the pair.

relations.myth: Council in the besieged Trojan camp
relations.note: Serestus shares the command and council setting with the pair.
Salius competes against Nisus and Euryalus in the footrace.

relations.myth: Nisus obstructs Salius during the footrace
relations.note: Nisus deliberately trips Salius so that Euryalus can win.
Diores competes with the pair and benefits from Salius’ fall.
Helymus competes with the pair and passes Salius after his fall.
Patron competes against Nisus and Euryalus in the footrace.
Panopes competes against Nisus and Euryalus in the footrace.
Acestes is the Sicilian host and ruler associated with the games.
Euryalus is the son of Opheltes, who raised him amid war.
Nisus is explicitly identified by the patronymic Hyrtacides.
Nisus invokes Jupiter or any god favoring his plan; none visibly intervenes.
Nisus prays to her to guide his missiles; both throws strike.
Nisus personifies Fortune as potentially preventing Euryalus from burying him.

relations.myth: Night raid against the Rutulian camp
relations.note: They massacre Turnus’ sleeping troops; his army later displays their severed heads.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Nisus kills Turnus’ sleeping kingly augur.
Euryalus takes Rhamnes’ phalerae and golden-studded belt.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Nisus kills Remus’ attendants and then decapitates Remus.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Nisus kills Lamyrus while he sleeps.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Nisus kills Lamus while he sleeps.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Nisus kills the handsome young Serranus after his drinking and gaming.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Euryalus kills Fadus during the night raid.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Euryalus kills Herbesus during the night raid.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Euryalus kills Abaris during the night raid.

relations.myth: Massacre in the sleeping Rutulian camp
relations.note: Euryalus kills Rhoetus as he rises from hiding behind a bowl.

relations.myth: Euryalus takes the fatal crested helmet
relations.note: Euryalus steals and wears Messapus’ helmet, whose reflection exposes him.
Volcens kills Euryalus despite Nisus claiming sole responsibility.
Nisus drives his sword into Volcens’ mouth before dying.
Nisus kills Sulmo with his first missile from concealment.
Nisus kills Tagus with his second missile.
